_source: Hand-entered 2026-11-22. Exemptions, indexing (CT, ME, NY, RI, DC), and portability (HI, MD) from estate-inheritance-taxes.html (Tax Foundation, as of October 1, 2026). Each state's method and brackets come from its own statute or form, named in the entry's source: excess (brackets on the estate above the exemption), whole (brackets on the whole estate, 0% below the exemption), credit (the old federal state death tax credit table, parsed from usc26-2011-2012.txt, on the estate less $60,000, less the table tax on the exemption), ny (the whole-estate table with the 105% phase-out of the credit), md, and il. Rows are [start, published tax at the start, marginal rate]; 21_build_rules.py checks each published tax against the rows before it. Inheritance tax rates by heir class are each state's statutory class rates (PA 4.5% lineal, 12% siblings, 15% others; NE 1% over $100,000, 11% over $40,000 for collateral relatives, 15% over $25,000 others, siblings in the 1% class; NJ and KY exempt children, siblings at 11% and 4% at the low end, others 15% and 6%; MD exempts children and siblings, others 10%).

CT.source: Tax Foundation table (flat 12% above the exclusion, which matches the federal exemption)

HI.source: hi-m6ins.pdf: Hawaii Form M-6 instructions, tax rate schedule as of January 1, 2020, on the net taxable estate (after the exclusion)

IL.source: il-estate-fact-sheet.pdf (Illinois Attorney General): the lesser of the 26 U.S.C. 2011 credit and 40% of the estate over $4,000,000, each with the Illinois tax itself deducted from the estate (interrelated); the fact sheet's $5,000,000 estate owes $285,714

ME.source: me-36-4103.html: 36 M.R.S. section 4103(1), on the excess over the Maine exclusion amount

MD.source: md-estate-tip42.pdf (Register of Wills tip 42): the 26 U.S.C. 2011 credit on the taxable estate less $60,000, capped at 16% of the excess over the exemption

MA.source: usc26-2011-2012.txt (26 U.S.C. 2011(b) as of 2012, the table Massachusetts freezes) on the taxable estate less $60,000, less a credit of $99,600, the table tax on $2,000,000 (M.G.L. c. 65C, 2A; checked against published examples: $2.5M owes $39,200, $5M owes $292,000)

MN.source: mn-291.03.html (Minn. Stat. 291.03 subd. 1(b), 2018 on) on the Minnesota taxable estate, which mn-291.016.html (subd. 3) reduces by the exclusion amount

NY.source: ny-et706.pdf (Form ET-706 page 6 tax table, on the whole New York taxable estate) and ny-et706i.pdf (line 3, the applicable credit: the whole tax up to the exclusion, the tax on the exclusion times 1 less the excess over 5% of it up to 105%, none above)

OR.source: ors-118.html: ORS 118.010(4), on the whole Oregon taxable estate

RI.source: usc26-2011-2012.txt on the taxable estate less $60,000, less a credit equal to the table tax on the exemption ($87,940 in 2026 for $1,838,056, Division of Taxation ADV 2025-27; published examples $3M owes $94,060, $5M owes $303,660)

WA.source: rcw-83.100.040.html: RCW 83.100.040(2)(a)(iii), deaths on or after July 1, 2026 (the 35% table of (ii) ran July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026), on the Washington taxable estate after the exclusion

DC.source: dc-47-3702.html: D.C. Code 47-3702(a-1)(1): 0% up to the zero bracket amount (the exemption), each dollar above it at the rate of the bracket it falls in by the whole taxable estate
